name: FairTix Smart Support Triage
description: Automated customer support system that classifies incoming support emails into categories (FAQ, Account, Payment, Technical, Resale, Feedback) and either generates AI-powered FAQ responses or routes complex issues to human agents.
trigger: Scheduled polling every minute for new Gmail messages with subject containing 'Support Request'
coreLogic: 1) Polls Gmail for new support requests 2) Uses Claude AI to classify messages into 6 categories with sentiment analysis 3) For FAQ questions, retrieves knowledge base content from Google Docs and generates personalized responses 4) Updates tracking spreadsheet with classification data 5) Sends automated responses for FAQ or alerts human support team for complex issues
businessContext: FairTix operates a fair ticket marketplace that eliminates bots and scalping through a lottery-based queue system. This workflow is their primary customer support automation, handling the intake and initial triage of all support requests. The 6-category classification system (FAQ, Account/Verification, Payment/Billing, Technical/Bug, Resale/Transfer, Feedback) reveals FairTix's core business operations and common customer touchpoints. The detailed classification prompts show they deal with fair queue mechanics, verification processes, payment issues, and resale policies — all critical to maintaining trust in their anti-scalping marketplace.
sideEffects: sends automated email responses to customers

impactProposal.reasoning: This is the primary customer support automation for a marketplace that depends entirely on customer trust. FairTix's business model (anti-scalping, fair pricing) means customer support quality directly impacts brand reputation and user retention. Failed automation means customers don't get timely responses about account issues, payment problems, or ticket delivery — all trust-eroding scenarios.

businessBrief: Automatically triages all customer support requests, instantly resolving FAQ questions with AI-generated responses while ensuring complex issues reach human agents.
timeSavingsEstimate: ~8-12 minutes per FAQ response at scale — eliminates manual email reading, knowledge base searching, and response composition. With 43 executions, potentially saving 6-9 hours of support agent time. Confidence: benchmark-based.
revenueImpactEstimate: High indirect impact — fast support response times are critical for marketplace trust and customer retention. Each delayed response to payment/verification issues risks customer churn. The automated FAQ responses maintain customer confidence during high-volume periods. Confidence: benchmark-based.
failureImpact: Support emails go unprocessed, creating a backlog of customer issues. FAQ questions that should resolve in minutes take hours or days. Payment and verification issues escalate unnecessarily. Customer trust erodes as response times increase. Support team gets overwhelmed with routine questions they could have avoided.
dataIn: Gmail messages with 'Support Request' in subject line containing customer questions, complaints, or feedback
dataOut: Classified support tickets with category/sentiment metadata, automated email responses for FAQ questions, human support alerts for complex issues

technicalEvidence.errorHandling: Mixed resilience. Most nodes use default retryOnFail: false. One node ('Notify Support Team') has explicit onError: continueErrorOutput, allowing graceful degradation if support alerts fail. No error workflow linked.
technicalEvidence.triggerInterval: Every 1 minute polling for new Gmail messages
technicalEvidence.versionCount: 135 iterations — extremely high, indicating active development and iteration
keyFindings: Workflow is inactive despite 135 versions — suggests development/testing phase
